top.title: Today in Motorsport History, November 6: Melandri Beat Hayden by 0.097s at Valencia in 2005 as Rossi Charged From 15th to Third
top.description: A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. Photo: Byron Sullivan / Pexels Marco Melandri beat Nicky Hayden by 0.097 seconds at Valencia 21 years ago today, on November 6, 2005, in the last race of a MotoGP season whose champion had already been settled. Valentino Rossi, who clinched his fifth straight premier-class title at Sepang six weeks earlier, started 15th after a qualifying crash and still finished third. The 2005 Valencia MotoGP finale was a race with nothing on the line for the title, and it still produced one of the closest finishes of the year. A title already decided, a runner-up fight still open Rossi wrapped up the 2005 championship at the Malaysian Grand Prix on September 25, finishing second to Loris Capirossi while his only remaining challenger, Max Biaggi, ended up sixth. It was his fifth consecutive premier-class crown (one in 500cc and four in MotoGP) and his seventh world title overall, according to Crash.net’s race report . That left second place in the standings as the live fight, and it was between two Hondas. Melandri arrived having won in Turkey the race before. He had climbed from 15th in the 2003 standings and 12th in 2004, and another win would secure second place in the championship. Hayden, the Repsol Honda rider, was chasing his best season yet after finishing fifth and eighth in his first two years in the class. What happened at Valencia Fact Detail Date Sunday, November 6, 2005 Event Valencian Community Grand Prix, final round of the 2005 MotoGP season Circuit Circuit Ricardo Tormo, Valencia, Spain MotoGP pole Sete Gibernau (1:31.874) Winner Marco Melandri, Movistar Honda (46:58.152) Margin 0.097s over Nicky Hayden, Repsol Honda Third Valentino Rossi, Yamaha, from 15th on the grid (+2.959s) Attendance 124,520, reported as a sell-out 2005 Valencian Community Grand Prix, MotoGP class. Sources: Crash.net race report; Wikipedia race entry; Road Racing World. Gibernau took pole for the fifth time that season, but his race was over within a few laps with an engine failure. Melandri led from the first corner and Hayden stayed on his tail for the whole 30 laps, on a circuit where overtaking is hard. Melandri opened a small gap, then had a bobble before the final corner that let Hayden close right up. Hayden went for the pass on the exit, and Melandri held his line to take the win. Melandri said afterward it was “a dream come true,” per Road Racing World . A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. He was up five places at the first corner and eighth by the end of lap one, then moved into third on lap six. top.title: ‘The Bad Kinda Nepotism,’ ‘This Is So Lame’ – NBA Fans Enraged By Lakers’ Owner Bob Iger’s Son Will’s Latest Move
top.description: ‘The Bad Kinda Nepotism,’ ‘This Is So Lame’ - NBA Fans Enraged By Lakers’ Owner Bob Iger’s Son Will’s Latest Move The Los Angeles Lakers are waiting on new ownership after former Disney CEO Bob Iger and Josh Kushner agreed in August to buy the franchise. Now Iger’s son is set to call games for the team’s G League affiliate, which opens its first season in the Coachella Valley on Friday night. ESPN’s Dave McMenamin relayed the Coachella Valley Lakers’ announcement Thursday that Will Iger will broadcast the team’s games this season. Fans responded by questioning the family connection. Will Iger Joins Coachella Valley Lakers Broadcasts Alongside A.C. Green Will Iger will handle the play-by-play in 2026-27, with A.C. Green beside him as the analyst. Green, who won three championships with the Lakers, did the same job when the team played as the South Bay Lakers. Will Iger’s first broadcast for the club is the season opener against the Salt Lake City Stars. McMenamin led with the family tie when he passed the team’s news along: “Will Iger, the son of incoming Lakers co-owner Bob Iger, will be broadcasting games for LAL’s G League affiliate this season, the Coachella Valley Lakers announced.” The reaction kept returning to the father-son connection, and the word nepotism came up more than once. Less than 20 minutes after McMenamin’s post, one fan wrote, “This the bad kinda nepotism btw.” Another fan saw the hire as a sign of something broader than one G League broadcast booth: “It’s amazing that we’ve gotten to a spot where people don’t even bother to hide the nepotism anymore. It’s become so normalized.” Will Iger does bring play-by-play experience to the role. Before this hire, he called Austin Spurs games, starting in early 2025 for Spurs Sports & Entertainment on FanDuel Sports Network Southwest, and worked some San Antonio FC home matches as well. That job began more than a year before his father agreed to buy into the Lakers. He has called Indoor Football League games since April. His résumé also includes Columbia and Hofstra athletics, high school games in the Austin area and analyst work on The Bounce, the Dallas Mavericks’ weekly show. top.title: Lions Trade Idea Could Bring Former Starting Cornerback Back to Detroit
top.description: The Detroit Lions are running out of time to strengthen their secondary before the November 10 NFL trade deadline, but one intriguing possibility could bring a familiar face back to the Motor City. And it’s a player Brad Holmes once traded to acquire. Carlton Davis III , who started 13 games for Detroit during the 2024 season before departing in free agency, has surfaced in NFL trade speculation involving the New England Patriots. According to NFL insider Albert Breer, Davis is among the veterans New England could consider moving before Tuesday’s deadline. That creates an interesting hypothetical reunion for a Lions team still searching for dependable outside cornerback help. But would the Patriots actually trade him, and could Detroit afford to bring him back? Jun 10, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Carlton Davis III (7) speaks to the media after minicamp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) NFL Insider Identifies Carlton Davis as Possible Trade Candidate During a recent appearance on NBC Sports Boston, Breer discussed New England’s potential willingness to move veteran players as the organization considers its long-term roster construction. As Breer explained while discussing the Patriots’ trade possibilities , Davis could become a candidate because of New England’s desire to get younger and accumulate draft capital. The Patriots have several expensive veterans on their roster, and Breer suggested that moving Davis or defensive tackle Christian Barmore wouldn’t necessarily be surprising. However, there’s an important distinction between the two situations. Breer indicated that New England has had trade conversations involving Barmore, while Davis was identified as someone who could potentially become available. There is no confirmed report that the Lions have contacted New England about Davis or that the Patriots have offered him to Detroit. For now, a reunion remains a hypothetical trade idea rather than a developing negotiation. Carlton Davis Already Knows What It Takes to Play in Detroit The biggest argument for bringing Davis back is simple. The Lions already know exactly what they’re getting. Detroit acquired Davis from Tampa Bay in March 2024, surrendering a third-round draft pick while receiving two sixth-round selections as part of the deal. The veteran immediately became an important part of Detroit’s secondary, starting 13 games and recording 56 tackles, two interceptions, and 11 passes defended before a broken jaw ended his season. His physical coverage style fit what the Lions wanted defensively, and his willingness to challenge opposing receivers made him a valuable presence on the outside. Former Lions cornerback Darius Slay even questioned Detroit’s decision to let Davis leave. top.title: Knueppel Injury Deal Another Blow To Hornets’ NBA Cup Hopes
top.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are in trouble again. Friday’s NBA Cup game versus the Boston Celtics saw Kon Knueppel ruled out just one day after he finally returned to the court. This news comes straight from the official injury report released Thursday. The second-year sharpshooter played less than six minutes on Wednesday before leaving with a left hamstring strain. Now he sits on the sidelines while the Celtics prepare to visit Spectrum Center. Knueppel’s absence is a disaster for a team already reeling. The 21-year-old missed the first eight games of the season due to the exact same injury. He was supposed to be the spark for an offense that has struggled to find rhythm. Instead, his comeback lasted less than one quarter. Coach Charles Lee offered no timeline for his return after the loss to Brooklyn. “No, I don’t have an update yet,” Lee said afterward, according to Yahoo Sports . A Deep Roster for Boston While Charlotte watches its young star sit, Boston looks ready to roll without its own top guy. Jayson Tatum rested on Wednesday but is expected to play Friday. The Celtics have already proven they can win even when their best player sits out. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night without Tatum. Paul George dropped 25 points and Derrick White added 24 to lead the way. Derrick White stepped up when Payton Pritchard also left the game early with an eye injury. White said his mindset changed when key players went down. “Obviously with JT out and then Payton going out too, I had a little bit more aggressive mind-set,” White said, according to Yahoo Sports . The Celtics believe their depth will carry them through the four-game road trip starting in Charlotte. Hornets Stuck in a Rut Charlotte has lost five games in a row and needs a win badly. They started the season strong with three wins in their first four games but have fallen apart since. The injury to Knueppel makes it nearly impossible to stop Boston’s offense. Brandon Miller struggled mightily on Wednesday, shooting just 2-for-15 from the field. Coach Lee noted that Miller’s defensive effort was still there despite the offensive woes. The Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla praised Paul George’s recent performance. “We need the best version of him for us to be a great team, and I think you were able to see that (Wednesday),” Mazzulla said, according to CBS Sports . Boston enters Friday with a 6-2 record. They are looking to extend their winning streak against a Hornets team that has no answers right now. The loss of Knueppel just confirms what everyone already fears: Charlotte is in deep trouble.

top.title: Alvaro Arbeloa beams as Fulham teenage sensation Josh King earns maiden England call-up from Thomas Tuchel
top.description: Coventry City v Fulham - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has hailed Josh King as the "pride" of the club after the teenage midfielder was handed a shock maiden call-up to the England senior squad. The 19-year-old academy graduate has been selected by Thomas Tuchel for upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain, marking a historic rise for the Craven Cottage starlet. Arbeloa hails Fulham’s rising star Arbeloa could not hide his delight after watching one of his brightest talents reach the international stage. The former Real Madrid defender turned manager spoke glowingly of the teenager, who has become the first Fulham outfield player to be selected for the Three Lions since Bobby Zamora. The call-up represents a massive milestone for a player who has spent more than a decade developing within the club's youth system. "This is a special moment for him, for us as a club and obviously for our supporters. I think Josh is the pride of our club and our supporters. He came to this club when he was eight years old. And now, when you look at him, how he’s playing, how he’s performing, we are really proud of him. So I think it’s a big step for him. I’m so happy for him because he’s a very humble kid," Arbeloa told Sky Sports . High praise paired with a reality check The Fulham boss believes this is only the beginning for the versatile midfielder, who has already travelled with the senior national team previously without making an appearance. Yet despite beaming with pride over his role in nurturing one of the club's brightest prospects, Arbeloa was quick to sound a vital note of caution, urging the rising star to keep his feet firmly planted on the ground. "You can see every day he wants to improve, he wants to work, he wants to become a better player every day. So I think it’s a special day for him and for all of us. I think he’s on the way to become a star; a very, very important player in this world. I’m so happy that I coached him, helped him to develop and reach his level. But he needs to stay humble like he is," Arbeloa noted. Tuchel explains the shock selection Tuchel has clearly been impressed by more than just the technical ability shown by the 19-year-old during his breakthrough season. The German tactician, who is preparing his side for high-stakes Nations League matches, suggested that King’s character played a pivotal role in his inclusion. While the squad features established stars, Tuchel is keen to reward those showing the right mentality in training and domestic competition. "He is just a fantastic character. top.title: Sam Mewis makes her picks for 2026 NWSL champion, MVP
top.description: The NWSL playoffs begin this weekend with four quarterfinal matchups: San Diego Wave vs. Utah Royals (Friday, Nov. 6), Kansas City Current vs. Angel City FC (Saturday, Nov. 7), Gotham FC vs. Seattle Reign (Sunday, Nov. 8) and Washington Spirit vs. Portland Thorns (Sunday, Nov. 8). Former U.S. women's national team star Sam Mewis, who hosts “The Women’s Game” podcast for the Men In Blazers network, said there’s one particular match she has circled on her calendar. “Kansas City versus Angel City, I had that circled the second that seeding got finalized,” Mewis told USA TODAY Sports in an interview on Nov. 5. “I feel that both teams are actually in really great form coming into playoffs. Among the top teams, I wouldn't want to play against either team. A few of us were saying it's kind of a bummer that this is a first-round game because it feels like a really big one.” Fourth-seeded Kansas City will host the quarterfinal at CPKC Stadium, where the Current have a 32-match regular-season unbeaten streak dating back to July 6, 2024. The magic might not extend to the playoffs, though; the Current lost at home in the 2025 quarterfinals to eventual champion Gotham. Fifth-seeded Angel City , meanwhile, has been on a tear since firing head coach Alexander Straus in June. Days after the coaching change, Angel City also made a mid-season trade with Kansas City to acquire attacker Ally Sentnor, who will face off against her former club in the quarterfinal. Under interim coach Leif Gunnar Smerud, Angel City went undefeated in its final 10 regular-season matches. “There's that expression, the 'new manager bump,’” Mewis said. “Things that were stagnant or not working, players suddenly feel the freedom to do things a little bit differently or respond in a way that they maybe weren't supposed to before. But I think what we're seeing with Angel City is actually really unique, and it feels like everything has come together recently.” Mewis, a three-time NWSL champion with the Western New York Flash and North Carolina Courage, said momentum is an important factor in the postseason. That could be results-based momentum, like San Diego going undefeated in its last seven games and locking up the No. 2 seed. Or it could be emotional momentum, like Seattle playing in honor of captain Jess Fishlock, who plans to retire at the end of the season. As volatile as the playoffs can be, Mewis is predicting that the top two seeded teams will reach the NWSL title game: defending champions and 2026 NWSL Shield winners Gotham FC — whose roster includes Mewis’ sister-in-law Sam Kerr and several USWNT players — and the San Diego Wave. top.title: As LIV Golf burned through cash, a lot of people made a lot of money
top.description: LIV Golf is shutting down after the investment firm that considered giving it $300 million withdrew its offer, forcing the league to begin liquidating its assets. LIV attorney Matthew Williams confirmed Thursday in New Jersey Bankruptcy Court the league will start selling its assets Monday after BC Partners decided it would not invest in LIV 2.0. Why did LIV Golf fail? Inside the nearly $6 billion experiment gone wrong The beginning of the end for the league created by Greg Norman as a competitor to the PGA Tour was when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund decided in April it could not continue to bankroll a business that offered nothing in return. And it took burning more than $5 billion for the PIF to realize that. Since then, golfers surely tired of CEO Scott O'Neil's outrageous claims and promises, all the while making sure he was taken care of as the ship was sinking. One by one, LIV's biggest assets — its players — bailed. Jumping into a future of uncertainty after being part of the money grab. All the while, O'Neil kept up the charade. After PIF pulled the plug seven months ago, O'Neil said LIV would do "what we do best: putting on the most compelling show in sports." One month ago, he said he believed deeply in the future of LIV and would build something distinctive alongside their players. "We’re delivering on our major milestones," he said. Social media reacts: Here's what people are saying about LIV Golf's demise LIV and BC Partners were seeking 30 to 40 players to compete next season. The Financial Times reported Wednesday about 30 players were currently committed and about 10 were undecided. Marquee names such as Brooks Koepka, Patrick Reed, Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Tyrrell Hatton had departed (Koepka and Reed started the trend early this year). Others such as Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Dustin Johnson were among 19 players whose contracts were allowed to be rejected amid bankruptcy and the restructuring process. DeChambeau appeared to be the last holdout, saying on a podcast Oct. 2 he believed LIV 2.0 can make "full financial sense” and hoped it would last forever. LIV indicated it had between $100 million and $500 million in assets and $500 million to $1 billion in liabilities. Lawsuits were piling up from contractors and vendors owed more than $4 million for work this year. That list included Fresh Tape Media, which produced LIV's preseason media days in January held at the Palm Beach County Convention Center. Additionally, 27 players were stiffed out of a combined $64.2 million. O’Neil, though, received more than $13.6 million in payroll, bonuses, benefits, retention payments and expense reimbursements from Sept. 2025 through Aug. 2026. LIV filed for bankruptcy Sept. 8. top.title: Ex-Gunner reflects on Arsenal spell ahead of Emirates return with Hull
top.description: Ex-Gunner reflects on Arsenal spell ahead of Emirates return with Hull Hull City’s Brooke Norton-Cuffy has reflected positively on his time with Arsenal, but he’ll be playing to win with his new side on Saturday. Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images Former Arsenal academy youngster Brooke Norton-Cuffy returned to England to play in the Premier League this summer, joining Hull City from Genoa . The move was a positive one from an Arsenal perspective, allowing them to cash in on the sell-on clause in Norton-Cuffy’s contract. The Gunners reportedly netted around £2.4m from the deal. But the downside is obviously that Arsenal will now have to play against Norton-Cuffy, with the 22-year-old set to make his first appearance against his old club in their Premier League clash on Saturday. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images Speaking ahead of the game, Norton-Cuffy insisted he still has many positive memories of his time in north London, although he’ll be returning to the Emirates Stadium looking for three points for Hull. “I look back at my time at Arsenal with fond memor­ies,” Norton-Cuffy said . “I learned a lot. I went from a boy to a man there. “They will have a lot of the ball, but we set up to go into every game to try and win it. I know our team is always going to be on the front foot, aggress­ive, and try­ing to win games.” Photo by George Wood/Getty Images Norton-Cuffy never made a senior competitive debut with Arsenal, despite showing a lot of promise and playing for the academy all the way up to the u21s. Rather than integrating the right-back with the senior side, Arsenal opted to send him out on various loans to Lincoln City , Rotherham United , Coventry City , and Millwall . Those spells went well enough to earn the player that move to Serie A side Genoa, and eventually back to the Premier League. top.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?

Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills. These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. nigeria.title: INEC: 116,745 newly registered voters yet to collect PVCs in Lagos
nigeria.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State says 116,745 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) of newly registered voters are yet to be collected. The Administrative Secretary of INEC in Lagos, Mrs Adenike Tadese, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday. Tadese said that the commission had received 177,295 PVCs belonging to eligible residents registered during Phase One of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise in 2025. She said the commission’s weekly update as of Monday showed that 60,550 PVCs had been collected by their owners, leaving 116,745 cards awaiting collection. According to her, the uncollected cards represent a significant number of eligible voters who should collect their PVCs to exercise their franchise in the 2027 general elections. She said the cards were available for collection at the various local government offices of the commission across the state. “The cards are available for collection by their owners, not by proxy, at the various local government offices of the commission in Lagos,” she said. Tadese urged stakeholders to mobilise both old registrants who have not collected their cards and those who participated in the 2025 CVR exercise to collect their PVCs. She said the cards were still lying at INEC offices and appealed to their owners to collect them before the collection window closed ahead of the forthcoming elections. The INEC official also disclosed that PVCs belonging to eligible residents who registered during the 2026 CVR exercise before its closure would soon be ready for collection. Tadese, however, urged eligible registered voters to maintain orderliness during the collection of their PVCs. She reaffirmed the commission’s readiness to conduct free, fair and credible elections that would be acceptable to all stakeholders in the state. nigeria.title: ANC gets 30% in South Africa’s election, partial results show
nigeria.description: South Africa’s once-dominant African National Congress was headed for its worst-ever election performance Friday with about a third of support after 80 percent of the votes from local government polls had been counted. Wednesday’s municipal elections were dominated by concerns over failing water and power supplies in one of Africa’s wealthiest nations which became a democracy in 1994 when the ANC took power. With final results expected by Sunday, the election authority dashboard showed the ANC was still the largest party with 31.8 percent of votes after 80 percent had been counted. Projections released Thursday by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), a state-funded research body, put its support at nearly 32 percent. This was its lowest score yet for the party after it secured just over 40 percent at the 2024 national polls and 46 percent at the previous municipal elections in 2021. At the heart of South Africa’s anti-apartheid struggle, the ANC — the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela — took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004. “This is the most severe result that the ANC would have feared,” political analyst Daniel Silke told AFP. “It’s the ANC’s worst result in history.” “It will undermine its ability to exert authority across South Africa, not just at a local level, but frankly at a national level as well,” he told AFP. “And opposition parties will be smelling blood when it comes to the next election in 2029.” The party now led by President Cyril Ramaphosa has borne the brunt of criticism about years of municipal mismanagement that have left South Africans grappling with failing water supplies, persistent power cuts and crumbling public services. The pro-business, centre-right Democratic Alliance (DA) was placing second with 24.2 percent of votes, according to the 80 percent count. nigeria.title: Family Sues Google Over Teenager’s Suicide-Related AI Chats On School Computer
nigeria.description: The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer. Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant’s low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world. The teenager, identified by the name Emma, was not able to access Google’s Gemini app, nor OpenAI’s ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google’s search engine, which contains AI-powered tools. Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students. Google on March 21, 2023 invited people in the United States and Britain to test its AI chatbot, known as Bard, as it scrambles to catch up with Microsoft-backed ChatGPT. (Photo by Pau BARRENA / AFP) “Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they’re interacting with AI,” Andrew Liddell, one of the family’s attorneys, told AFP on Thursday. The complaint alleges that Emma had been a “happy 13-year-old girl” in North Carolina who received great grades, played music and participated in Girl Scouts. Despite “no history” of mental illness, within months of using Google’s AI-powered search on her school laptop, she began a “quiet spiral into a severe psychological crisis” according to the complaint. On March 17, the school’s monitoring software flagged a document titled “Funeral,” and the school notified her parents. Her mother then saw Emma writing a farewell letter in real-time after logging into her daughter’s account, and her father intervened. “We are reviewing the claims in the lawsuit and we take this very seriously,” Google spokesperson Jose Castaneda told AFP. Google argues that AI mode includes safeguards against self-harm and attempts to bypass them. But Emma “was able to keep going back over and over and over again,” Liddle said. “Whatever safeguards they think they put in place were obviously insufficient.” Developers of fast-evolving AI technology are facing a litany of similar lawsuits in the US. OpenAI faces several wrongful death suits, including from the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine, a teenager who committed suicide allegedly using methods advised by ChatGPT. Google and the startup Character.AI agreed in January to settle several lawsuits filed by families of teenagers out of court. On Wednesday, Google, TikTok and Meta each separately sued California to block a law that prohibits social media companies from providing addictive features to users under 16. Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law in September, and it goes into effect on January 1, 2027. nigeria.description: Why Africa’s newest financial institution must turn energy resources into energy access, industrial growth and lasting prosperity. By Ambassador Gabriel Aduda Chief Insight Officer, World Energy Council Nigeria Former Federal Permanent Secretary and Former OPEC Governor for Nigeria The formal establishment of the Africa Energy Bank (AEB) by the African Petroleum Producers’ Organisation (APPO) and the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), announced in Abuja on 31 October 2026, marks an important step towards African-led energy finance. The Bank has authorised capital of US$5 billion and is intended to finance projects across the energy value chain. Its establishment comes as traditional lenders reassess fossil fuel exposure, while African countries face urgent needs for electricity, clean cooking, infrastructure and industrial investment (APPO, 31 October 2026). The scale of the challenge is clear. The International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates that about 600 million people in Africa lack electricity and more than one billion lack access to clean cooking (IEA, 2025). It also estimates that meeting Africa’s energy and climate goals will require annual investment exceeding US$200 billion by 2030 (IEA, 2024). The central question is whether the AEB can help meet these needs while strengthening energy security, affordability and sustainability. Its success will depend not only on the capital it mobilises, but on the quality of its governance, investments and development outcomes. But its lasting relevance should not be measured only by how much oil and gas production it finances. A bank focused narrowly on extraction would risk repeating a long-standing pattern: exporting raw resources while importing refined products, equipment, technology and manufactured goods. Africa’s challenge is to convert energy resources into reliable power, competitive industries, jobs, local expertise and improved living standards. A gas project, for example, should be assessed not only by production and export revenues, but also by its potential contribution to electricity, fertiliser, petrochemicals and industrial development. Renewable generation should be considered alongside the transmission, storage and distribution systems needed to deliver power reliably and affordably. nigeria.description: A US federal judge blocked President Donald Trump’s massive triumphal arch project on Thursday, casting doubt over the future of the project hours after it was green-lit by a public commission. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, who is overseeing the case, ruled that the Trump administration cannot start construction on the arch for two weeks while the court considers challenges to its legality. The National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) had voted 8-4 to approve the project earlier Thursday, despite hearing hours of testimony from dozens of furious opponents who questioned its legality and purpose. Chief among the complaints was the location of the 250-foot (76-meter) tall structure: adjacent to the hallowed Arlington National Cemetery, the final resting place for hundreds of thousands of American service members. The giant arch would be much taller than the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, its inspiration. It would also tower over the Lincoln Memorial, directly across the Potomac River. The four dissenting commissioners had called for the decision to be delayed, noting there were legal concerns, a lack of congressional appropriation to fund the project and questions about Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s claims of the arch’s military use. But the majority on the panel, which is controlled by Trump allies, voted against a delay and the Trump administration said it aimed to start work right away. Chutkan’s ruling sided with several veterans and the attorneys general of Washington and Virginia, who had sued seeking to halt construction of the arch. – ‘Illegal project’ – The arch is one of several projects launched by Trump in a bid to put his personal stamp on the capital, many of which have prompted legal challenges. They include a White House ballroom, for which Trump had an entire wing of the presidential mansion demolished. The Supreme Court ultimately ruled that the plaintiff who filed suit to halt the project did not have standing. Another is the repeated renovation of the Reflecting Pool, a massive rectangular water basin on the National Mall. Trump has also proposed revamping the East Potomac Golf Links, a historic waterfront Washington golf course, cutting down hundreds of trees before a judge halted the project. The location, a traffic circle currently covered in grass, is key to the Trump administration’s defense of the project. Proponents claim that Congress approved the construction of a monument at the site over a century ago. More than 100 people, often speaking as representatives of organizations, expressed their nearly unanimous opposition. Traders who bought the midterm rebound with borrowed money were the first forced out when stocks cracked at the open, and the bitcoin price never regained the $77,000 area that held as morning support. Nasdaq’s correction pulls crypto lower Wall Street set the tone. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% on Thursday and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Today in Motorsport History, November 6: Melandri Beat Hayden by 0.097s at Valencia in 2005 as Rossi Charged From 15th to Third
sports.description: A rider on a white sports bike. Illustrative image, not from the 2005 season finale. Photo: Byron Sullivan / Pexels Marco Melandri beat Nicky Hayden by 0.097 seconds at Valencia 21 years ago today, on November 6, 2005, in the last race of a MotoGP season whose champion had already been settled. Valentino Rossi, who clinched his fifth straight premier-class title at Sepang six weeks earlier, started 15th after a qualifying crash and still finished third. The 2005 Valencia MotoGP finale was a race with nothing on the line for the title, and it still produced one of the closest finishes of the year. A title already decided, a runner-up fight still open Rossi wrapped up the 2005 championship at the Malaysian Grand Prix on September 25, finishing second to Loris Capirossi while his only remaining challenger, Max Biaggi, ended up sixth. It was his fifth consecutive premier-class crown (one in 500cc and four in MotoGP) and his seventh world title overall, according to Crash.net’s race report . That left second place in the standings as the live fight, and it was between two Hondas. Melandri arrived having won in Turkey the race before. He had climbed from 15th in the 2003 standings and 12th in 2004, and another win would secure second place in the championship. Hayden, the Repsol Honda rider, was chasing his best season yet after finishing fifth and eighth in his first two years in the class. Melandri led from the first corner and Hayden stayed on his tail for the whole 30 laps, on a circuit where overtaking is hard. Melandri opened a small gap, then had a bobble before the final corner that let Hayden close right up. Hayden went for the pass on the exit, and Melandri held his line to take the win. sports.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets are in trouble again. Friday’s NBA Cup game versus the Boston Celtics saw Kon Knueppel ruled out just one day after he finally returned to the court. This news comes straight from the official injury report released Thursday. The second-year sharpshooter played less than six minutes on Wednesday before leaving with a left hamstring strain. Now he sits on the sidelines while the Celtics prepare to visit Spectrum Center. Knueppel’s absence is a disaster for a team already reeling. The 21-year-old missed the first eight games of the season due to the exact same injury. He was supposed to be the spark for an offense that has struggled to find rhythm. Instead, his comeback lasted less than one quarter. Coach Charles Lee offered no timeline for his return after the loss to Brooklyn. “No, I don’t have an update yet,” Lee said afterward, according to Yahoo Sports . A Deep Roster for Boston While Charlotte watches its young star sit, Boston looks ready to roll without its own top guy. Jayson Tatum rested on Wednesday but is expected to play Friday. The Celtics have already proven they can win even when their best player sits out. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks 109-102 on Wednesday night without Tatum. Paul George dropped 25 points and Derrick White added 24 to lead the way. Derrick White stepped up when Payton Pritchard also left the game early with an eye injury. White said his mindset changed when key players went down. “Obviously with JT out and then Payton going out too, I had a little bit more aggressive mind-set,” White said, according to Yahoo Sports . The Celtics believe their depth will carry them through the four-game road trip starting in Charlotte. Hornets Stuck in a Rut Charlotte has lost five games in a row and needs a win badly. They started the season strong with three wins in their first four games but have fallen apart since. The injury to Knueppel makes it nearly impossible to stop Boston’s offense. Brandon Miller struggled mightily on Wednesday, shooting just 2-for-15 from the field. Coach Lee noted that Miller’s defensive effort was still there despite the offensive woes. The Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla praised Paul George’s recent performance. “We need the best version of him for us to be a great team, and I think you were able to see that (Wednesday),” Mazzulla said, according to CBS Sports . Boston enters Friday with a 6-2 record. They are looking to extend their winning streak against a Hornets team that has no answers right now. The loss of Knueppel just confirms what everyone already fears: Charlotte is in deep trouble.

Inside the nearly $6 billion experiment gone wrong The beginning of the end for the league created by Greg Norman as a competitor to the PGA Tour was when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund decided in April it could not continue to bankroll a business that offered nothing in return. And it took burning more than $5 billion for the PIF to realize that. Since then, golfers surely tired of CEO Scott O'Neil's outrageous claims and promises, all the while making sure he was taken care of as the ship was sinking. One by one, LIV's biggest assets — its players — bailed. Jumping into a future of uncertainty after being part of the money grab. All the while, O'Neil kept up the charade. After PIF pulled the plug seven months ago, O'Neil said LIV would do "what we do best: putting on the most compelling show in sports." One month ago, he said he believed deeply in the future of LIV and would build something distinctive alongside their players. "We’re delivering on our major milestones," he said. The move was a positive one from an Arsenal perspective, allowing them to cash in on the sell-on clause in Norton-Cuffy’s contract. The Gunners reportedly netted around £2.4m from the deal. But the downside is obviously that Arsenal will now have to play against Norton-Cuffy, with the 22-year-old set to make his first appearance against his old club in their Premier League clash on Saturday. I know our team is always going to be on the front foot, aggress­ive, and try­ing to win games.” Photo by George Wood/Getty Images Norton-Cuffy never made a senior competitive debut with Arsenal, despite showing a lot of promise and playing for the academy all the way up to the u21s. technology.description: When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true It is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills. These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. technology.title: Bank of England pours cold water on AI productivity boom
technology.description: Despite the billions being thrown at artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered little in the way of productivity gains for UK businesses, according to the Bank of England. In its latest Monetary Policy Report , the central bank found that AI has increased UK productivity by an estimated 0.5 percent over the past three years. That works out to just 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points of additional annual productivity growth since early 2024, hardly the economic revolution Silicon Valley has been promising. "AI investment appears to be contributing somewhat to current demand strength, but so far there is only evidence of a modest AI-driven rise in UK productivity growth," the Bank said. Even industries supposedly best placed to benefit from the technology have little to boast about. Productivity growth has improved in AI-heavy sectors such as information and communications, but has yet to exceed pre-pandemic averages. That's not to say AI isn't doing anything for the British economy. The bank estimates that AI-related activity has accounted for just under a fifth of UK GDP growth since the beginning of 2026, though much of that appears to come from companies developing and deploying the technology rather than businesses becoming more productive by using it. "The contribution to growth from AI to date appears to reflect activity in the upstream development and implementation of AI technologies rather than broader gains from their adoption elsewhere in the economy," the report said. In other words, selling AI is proving rather more lucrative than actually using it, The bank also cautioned against giving AI too much credit for Britain's recent productivity improvements. Much of the increase appears to reflect businesses hiring fewer workers while output continues to grow, partly as companies unwind post-pandemic staffing decisions and respond to higher employment costs. And despite predictions that AI will make vast swathes of the workforce redundant, firms responding to the Bank's Decision Maker Panel survey reported virtually no overall impact on employment so far. The technology is, however, making some employers less inclined to hire new staff or replace those who leave. Other studies suggest businesses are still waiting for the payoff. A Gartner survey published last month found that while three-quarters of corporate board members expected AI to improve productivity and cut costs, just 3 percent of organizations had actually achieved their targets. Meanwhile, 38 percent were already over budget on AI spending, yet 85 percent planned to spend even more next year. Another study involving nearly 6,000 executives , published in February, found that more than 80 percent of firms had seen no discernible impact from AI on either employment or productivity. technology.title: UK ministers seek powers to investigate when AI agents are let off the leash
technology.description: The UK government is paving the way for rules requiring essential service operators and digital providers to guard against losing control of AI agents and report incidents when safeguards fail. An amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, which is passing through Parliament , would give ministers powers to regulate the deployment and reporting of agentic AI in certain organizations. The new clause was introduced during the bill's third reading in the House of Lords this week. In an explanatory note , ministers outlined plans for safeguards, notification of affected organizations, preservation of evidence, and government-led incident reviews. The measures would require consultation and parliamentary approval through secondary legislation. The move follows a series of incidents. Last month, OpenAI revealed that its agents repeatedly strayed beyond their intended scope , prompting the company to notify more than 100 organizations about the issues. That came after July's incident, in which an OpenAI agent accessed the internet and breached machine learning platform Hugging Face . The episode, and the potential for more damage from poorly designed AI agent deployments, have prompted MPs to question whether UK law can deal with such threats. Speaking to The Register , Stuart Davey, a partner at law firm Pinsent Masons, described the clause as "quite novel." Rather than directly imposing new duties, it would allow ministers to introduce rules and investigatory powers covering regulated organizations. Davey said that could include powers "to look where there has been such an AI agentic compromise or issue, and do some things... appoint inspectors, enter and search premises, seize and retain documents." Under the proposals, the minister could confer certain powers on regulators, requiring action from targeted organizations. Potentially affected organizations include gas and electricity suppliers, managed service providers, and cloud providers deploying AI agents for customers. Foundation model developers would not automatically fall within scope simply because they build the underlying technology. "Where there's a security or operational compromise in relation to a relevant network or information system, that would seem to capture those managed service providers or cloud computing providers who are using AI, and there's that loss of control," said Davey. He advised cloud and managed service providers to track whether the proposed measures become law. Evin McMullen, CEO and co-founder of AI identity and control infrastructure company AmanTrue, said the amendment recognizes loss of oversight or control as a security risk but does not itself impose new duties. "The amendment allows future regulations to introduce investigatory and enforcement powers where an incident involves an AI agent, targeting organizations running essential digital services," he said. technology.title: NHS wants a second opinion on Palantir's glowing self-assessments
technology.description: NHS England CEO Sir Jim Mackey plans to tell Palantir to clear future claims about its Federated Data Platform's benefits with his team – although he admits that could be difficult to enforce. Speaking to the Health and Social Care Committee this week, Labour MP Ben Coleman noted that NHS England had cautioned against attributing improvements directly to the platform, but said newly appointed Palantir UK senior vice president Tom Watson "is making claims that [Palantir] is making a difference, and that it's due to Palantir that changes are taking place." Responding, Mackey said he would write to Palantir and "tell them that they have to share with us and clear with us any benefits claimed in the future." But getting Palantir to comply could be another matter. "They should share them with us, but contractually, it looks hard to enforce," Mackey said. The planned letter follows repeated questions about the evidence NHS England and Palantir have used to promote the Federated Data Platform (FDP). NHS England awarded the £330 million contract to a Palantir-led consortium in November 2023 to help improve planning and efficiency. In July, campaign group Foxglove wrote to the UK health minister questioning figures used in Parliament to justify the contract. The Office for Statistics Regulation (OSR) also began examining the evidence. NHS England had said that as of June, 139 trusts used the platform, with 137 reporting benefits. It said an Inpatient Care Coordination Solution tool based on the FDP had helped hospitals perform procedures on an additional 111,589 patients. However, a Freedom of Information request later found that nearly a third of NHS trusts using Palantir's health data platform were performing fewer patient procedures than before it went live. The regulator noted that NHS England had published on its website a caveat saying that it could not "draw conclusions about cause and effect as other variables have not been controlled for." Last month, Watson, the former deputy leader of the Labour Party, sought to rebut what he described as misinformation about the FDP, repeating the statement that 137 trusts were already reporting benefits without mentioning the caveats. "That's a fair note of caution." technology.title: Britain's tech ambitions depend on minerals made in China, MPs warn
technology.description: Britain's ambitions for AI, advanced chips, and clean energy rest on mineral supply chains dominated by China, and MPs say they cannot establish whether ministers have a credible plan to reduce that dependence. The House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee has set ministers ten tests for securing critical minerals. Its verdict is hardly glowing – it cannot be confident the government passes any of them. The tests cover whether ministers know which industries and technologies need protecting, what minerals they require, where supplies could be disrupted, and how domestic production, overseas partnerships, skills, and financing will close the gaps. In a report published today , the committee warns that diversifying supplies will take ten to 15 years, and will require sustained investment and cooperation with allies. Completely cutting China out is neither realistic nor desirable, it says. Leaving Beijing with so much leverage is another matter. Critical minerals underpin everything from batteries and semiconductors to datacenters and military equipment. The designation reflects their economic or security importance and vulnerability to supply disruption, rather than membership of an especially exclusive geological club. The UK – like pretty much all major industrialized economies including the US, the EU, Japan, and India – is almost entirely dependent on imports of these materials and mineral product s. But digging up more ore outside China would solve only part of the problem. The bigger bottleneck is processing. Citing International Energy Agency figures, the committee says China is the leading refiner for 19 of 20 strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent. A different flag over the mine does not necessarily mean a different route through the refinery. The exposure extends beyond chips and batteries. As The Register reported in August , erbium is used to amplify signals in fiber-optic links, while yttrium goes into components including ceramic capacitors. IEEE Spectrum warned that China effectively monopolized the processing of both into the industrially usable materials manufacturers need. That concentration has already caused disruption. China's rare earth export controls in April 2025 , introduced following US tariffs, rippled through manufacturing supply chains and forced temporary automotive plant closures. British manufacturers can suffer even when Britain isn't the intended target. The committee also highlights gallium and germanium, used in advanced semiconductors for radar, communications, and electronic warfare. China accounts for 95 percent and 93 percent of their global production respectively, according to the report [PDF]. Beijing flexing its leverage over chip materials is not new. China announced export licensing requirements for gallium and germanium in July 2023 amid tightening Western restrictions on semiconductor technology. technology.title: Safari's Autofill feature may be distorting time
technology.description: The autofill feature of Apple's Safari browser appears to be suffering from a date handling error that occasionally leads it to supply an incorrect credit card expiration date when filling out forms. The supposed issue has been a sore spot for Apple customers dating back at least to 2017, when the author of an Apple Community forum post complained about changes to the month field in the Autofill credit card expiration date when moving between time zones. "I've noticed for the last year or so, whenever I travel from Eastern time zone (my home) to Central time zone or even Pacific time zone that my credit card expiration date month changes in Safari Autofill," the Safari user wrote. Another post in 2021 raised similar concerns. "I don't know how to reproduce this," the author wrote. "Every few months Safari on any of my devices changes the expiration month of all of my stored credit cards by decreasing the month by 1, for example instead of 10/2029 it changes it to 09/2029." Three years later, another person posting to Apple's Community forum reported the same issue. "For a few years now every time I use Autofill on my computer my credit cards (ALL of them) always have their expiration dates change one month earlier," the 2024 post says. "I thought it was just a glitch on my computer but I bought a new computer and didn't transfer anything from my old one and it is still doing it." An unrelated Autofill bug report from 2024 suggests that if there is an issue, it resides in Apple-owned Safari code rather than Safari's open source WebKit engine. Wherever the bug may reside, Safari's unreliable handling of credit card dates has kept a complaint-filled Reddit thread going for four years. And the reported month-shifting has been noted in other threads, too. The Register was unable to reproduce the described behavior, but a reader insists it's still a problem. "The Safari AutoFill feature sometimes fills in the credit card expiration date wrong," the reader explained. "My credit card expires in December, but sometimes Apple helpfully enters November." "To be clear, the card is stored correctly when inspected in Settings," our tipster added. "The off-by-one error only happens when filling out a form in Safari, and not consistently." One possible way this might happen is if the Safari Autofill code implemented the expiration date using Swift's DateComponent type and stored it as a Calendar object with UTC as the TimeZone identifier. Doing so would anchor the date to a specific time. If the date components were extracted in Pacific Time, the value would be represented as eight hours ahead (PST). So 9/1/2027 at 00:00 would appear as 8/31/2027 at 16:00. Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but we're told Apple's Help Desk – or "Helpless Desk" as our source put it – advised clearing the browser cache and re-entering details of the affected credit card. technology.title: Hospital gave very sick doctor a special PC for his personal, erm, pleasure
technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to a fresh edition of On Call, The Register 's weekly tale of tech support trials and tribulations that readers kindly share. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Mason," who told us he once worked at a hospital doing tech support for its research labs. "One of the labs was for a doctor who was one of the world's top organ transplant researchers" Mason told On Call. The doctor was also a voracious consumer of – ahem – adult entertainment, a habit that saw his PC and other machines around the lab often come down with a nasty case of malware. Mason got to clean that up, sometimes multiple times in a single week. The doctor's foibles were widely known around the hospital, as was the fact that his activities violated several workplace policies. Mason pointed this out to his boss every time he cleaned up a fresh malware outbreak but such was the doctor's status that management never intervened. And then the hospital was hit by a nasty cyber-worm that did a lot of damage. During the cleanup, Mason's colleagues found logs that showed the doctor's PC was the source of the infection, and that he had been indulging in his online hobby at the time the worm arrived. Mason assumed this would be the moment at which the doctor would finally be held accountable and face disciplinary action. Instead the doctor made a bargain with the IT department to henceforth use only a designated PC when pursuing – ahem – personal and/or intimate matters. And he would only use office PCs for actual work. The hospital's tech team rescued a PC from its e-waste pile for this job. "Get this thing going and deliver it to Doctor Pervert," Mason's boss ordered. By this stage, Mason had had enough. He escalated his protests, telling his boss that indulging this doctor was unprofessional, likely exposed the hospital to lawsuits, wasted IT department resources, and was just wrong. "What do you want to hear?" his boss replied. "The CIO told me do this or get another job." After Mason prepped that PC, he only needed to clean up malware about once a year – after the poor machine was so overrun with malware that it no longer served the doctor's purposes. Mason left the hospital while this PC was still in place. "You'll be shocked, no doubt, to learn that years later the doctor's graduate students filed a lawsuit," he told On Call. "And that the separate fun-time computer was one of the pieces of evidence that the hospital knew about his – ahem – proclivities and not just ignored them but facilitated them." technology.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
technology.description: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. Vendors of observability tools will be warming up their Indian sales teams today, because CERT-IN’s advice to Indian businesses includes improving their ability to log events, monitor for anomalies in real time, and send alerts. It also urged keeping test environments off the internet, and restricting access to cloud resources because CRAFTY FALCON is fond of using them to run its attacks.
